_comment_relayId: The relay's public identity, bound into the maker challenge so a signature for THIS relay can't be replayed to another. Set it to the relay's public hostname.
_comment_openRegistration: SECURE DEFAULT false = permissioned: only maker_ids in allowedMakers may register. Set true to let ANYONE run a maker and join (bring-your-own-maker). Reputation is relay-attested identity + self-reported stats; swaps are safe either way (non-custodial). NOTE: open mode is DoS-exposed; ed25519 identities are free, so ~maxPerIp source IPs can fill maxMakers and dominate /roster. buildRoster sorts the operator's defaultMaker first (its swap path is unaffected), but if you enable open mode consider per-subnet maker caps or proof-of-work at the edge.
_comment_allowedMakers: ed25519 maker_ids (64-hex) permitted when not open. Run `node src/main.js maker-id` in swap-maker to print your maker's id. Include your operator maker here.
_comment_defaultMaker: The operator maker_id a taker with no ?maker is routed to (legacy compatibility). Set to your operator maker's id.
_comment_vouched: Operator TRUST hints, { "<maker_id>": "<label>" } e.g. { "aca6...b51": "Operator" }. Shows a ✓ badge on that maker in the UI. Set ONLY by you here. A maker can NEVER self-claim it. It is a hint, not a safety guarantee (swaps are non-custodial regardless). Labels are capped at 24 chars, [A-Za-z0-9 ._-].
_comment_makerToken: OPTIONAL now: if set, an extra Bearer-token gate for the defaultMaker id only. Open/permissioned registration uses the ed25519 signature, not this.
_comment_allowedOrigins: If NON-EMPTY, a browser WS handshake is accepted only when its Origin header is in this list. WebSockets bypass the same-origin policy, so without this ANY page in a visitor's browser can open your relay from their IP and drive the protocol (drive-by cross-origin abuse that also spreads flooding across many residential IPs). List EVERY browser app that connects: your site AND any wallet, plus dev/preview origins, e.g. ["https://testnetswap.com", "https://testnetwallet.net"]. IMPORTANT: only browser Origins are checked. Non-browser clients (the maker over loopback, native/BYO wallets) send NO Origin and are ALWAYS allowed through - a page cannot forge or omit its Origin, so drive-by is still fully blocked, but your own maker is never rejected. (Setting a list that omits an origin blocks THAT browser app, not the maker.) Leave [] to accept any browser Origin.
_comment_maxPayloadBytes: 256 KiB. The XMR adaptor-swap 'bundle' message carries a cross-curve DLEQ proof (~114 KB); the old 64 KiB cap made the relay's ws server 1009-close the connection the instant a bundle was sent, so every XMR swap failed with 'recv timeout bundle'. HTLC messages are tiny, so this only matters once XMR is enabled.
_comment_trustProxyHops: Number of TRUSTED reverse-proxy hops in front of the relay (1 for the documented single Apache proxy). Behind a proxy this MUST be >= 1, or every client is seen as 127.0.0.1 and maxPerIp becomes a global cap. Set to 0 ONLY if the relay is exposed directly (else X-Forwarded-For is spoofable). TLS is provided by the proxy; a public relay MUST be behind WSS.
